entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:1
segments: In the plain over against the Red sea--Dizahab; "the plain" is the long narrow valley extending all the way from the sea of Galilee to the Red sea, in the lowest part of which the Dead sea lies.  The Israelites were in this plain opposite Jericho.  They are said to be "over against the Red sea," because they are in the northern part of the plain opposite to the Red sea, which lay at the other end of that plain. This plain is then further described as lying between Paran--the region about Kadesh--on the west, and Tophel on the east in the mountains of Moab.  Several places are then named which skirt the western border of this plain called the Arabah, or of the sea of Akabah, at which its southern extremity terminates.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:3
segments: Men who have spent their life in the service of God, as they draw near its close may often with great advantage recount the goodness of God, and repeat his commands to those around them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:4
segments: Sihon--and Og;

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:6
segments: Horeb; the general name of the mountains of which Sinai was one.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:7
segments: The mount of the Amorites; the mountainous region of Canaan, which the Israelites, if obedient to God, would have entered from its southern part near Kadesh.

The Amorites were properly the inhabitants of the mountains, but they are sometimes put in a general sense for all the Canaanitish tribes. 
 
  The plain; see note to

. 
 
  The hills; the mountainous part of Canaan. 
 
  The vale; the level region on the Mediterranean. 
 
  The south; the southern part of the land bordering on the desert. 
 
  The seaside; the coast of the Mediterranean. 
 
  Lebanon--Euphrates; the original grant extended thus far,
; but the northern and eastern part of this region was never permanently in the possession of the Israelites.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:8
segments: Unto your fathers;

vv 9-18. 
 
  Rulers over you;

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:11
segments: As good men draw near to heaven, they possess, and often manifest and unusual degree of the spirit of heaven, in earnest desires, fervent prayers, and benevolent efforts for the good of others.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:17
segments: Magistrates are God's ministers to execute that part of his government which concerns the temporal rights of men, and as such are bound to be candid and impartial; to decide and act in the fear nad love of God, and according to truth and duty.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:19
segments:
vv 19-21. 
 
  Kadesh-barnea;

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:21
segments: Great courage is needful in order to be willing, under all circumstances, to obey God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:22
segments:
vv 22-45. 
 
  Ye would not go up;

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:30
segments: None will have courage enough to obey God, except those who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:34
segments: God is angry with those who are afraid to obey him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:37
segments: To please God, men must be careful not to boast of their own power; or take the glory of what they do to themselves.  As they have nothing good but what God gives them, the glory of their doing good all belongs to him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:39
segments: Little children are objects of God's peculiar kindness and care; and though the sins of parents may occasion them great trouble, yet by loving and obeying their Father in heaven they may be delivered from all sorrow, and inherit pure and everlasting joy.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:44
segments: The Amorites; here a general name for the Canaanitish tribes.  In
, they are called Amalekites and Canaanites.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:45
segments: Men often weep in view of the evils they have brought on themselves, when it is too late to escape them.  They must trust in and obey God, if they would avoid deep and unavailing sorrow.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 1:46
segments: In Kadesh many days;
